purpose: Business-model validation of India's major metal-recycling companies against this repo's own trade data (metals_hsn4 4-digit import detail) and the CEEW solar-module-recycling economics. Tests one thesis: recycling businesses are viable exactly where reverse logistics already exist (lead/batteries), and the growth runway is the $8bn/yr of scrap India currently IMPORTS as feedstock.

sources.company_financials: yfinance .info TTM snapshots, retrieved 2026-08-03 (listed companies only)
sources.pv_recycling_economics: CEEW, 'How Much Does it Cost to Recycle a Solar Module in India?' (Kale & Tyagi, Nov 2025) + EU-India Technical Cooperation PV Waste/EPR report
sources.policy: DST Call for Proposals on Recovery & Recycling of End-of-Life Solar PV Panels/Modules; Ministry of Mines Rs.1,500 crore recycling incentive scheme under National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM)

thesis_anchors_from_trade_data_usd_milli.lead_net_position: net EXPORTER (+98) — the only base metal where India's circular loop has closed, via battery recycling

GRAVITA.NS.name: Gravita India Limited
GRAVITA.NS.model: Lead (primary), aluminium and plastic recycling; multinational smelting footprint (India + Africa + Central America); sells recycled ingots/alloys to battery and auto OEMs
GRAVITA.NS.validation: CONFIRMED at scale. Highest operating margin of the cohort (9.7%) and 42% revenue growth. Lead-centric model sits exactly on the one metal our trade data shows India net-exports — mature battery reverse-logistics is the moat, overseas plants add feedstock access India lacks.

POCL.NS.name: Pondy Oxides And Chemicals Limited
POCL.NS.model: Secondary lead smelting (battery scrap to refined lead/alloys), expanding into copper and plastics
POCL.NS.validation: CONFIRMED, fastest grower (+79% YoY). Thin 5.7% operating margin but 19% ROE — classic spread business earning returns on asset turnover, not markup. Copper diversification targets the $3.4bn imported-copper-scrap line.

NILE.NS.name: Nile Limited
NILE.NS.model: Secondary lead smelting; announced lithium-ion battery recycling subsidiary (NCMM-aligned)
NILE.NS.validation: CONFIRMED, most conservative balance sheet (D/E 3.8%, P/B 1.9 — cheapest of the cohort). Same lead-loop economics; LiB recycling is the NCMM option ticket.

NRL.NS.name: Nupur Recyclers Limited
NRL.NS.validation: PARTIAL. Growth is real (+49%) but 12% ROE at PE 53 / P/B 5.6 means the market is paying tomorrow's circular-economy price for today's spread business. Weakest risk-reward of the four.

CMR Green Technologies.model: India's largest metal recycler — aluminium & zinc die-casting alloys for auto OEMs; feedstock is substantially the $4.55bn/yr imported aluminium scrap line (HS 7602)
CMR Green Technologies.validation: Model validated by the import data (secondary aluminium demand is real and growing), but scale depends on imported scrap access — domestic ELV collection under NCMM is its structural unlock. Filed for IPO in 2022, withdrew; financials not publicly verifiable here.

Jain Metal Group.model: Non-ferrous recycling — copper, lead, aluminium scrap to high-purity ingots/granules
Jain Metal Group.validation: Copper leg sits on the strongest structural deficit in our data: refined copper imports $2.77bn and chapter-74 imports compounding at ~13%/yr since FY2018-19. Unlisted; financials not publicly verifiable here.

Ardee Industries.validation: Same validated lead-loop economics as the listed trio; LME brand approval supports the export leg that made India a net lead exporter. Unlisted; financials not publicly verifiable here.

sector_findings: The viable Indian recycling business today is a SPREAD business: 5-10% operating margins, returns earned via asset turnover (ROE ~12-19%), feedstock procurement is the dominant cost — the same 56-68% procurement-cost structure CEEW found makes solar recycling unviable at current module prices.

Every profitable listed recycler is lead-first. That is not a coincidence: lead-acid batteries are the only waste stream in India with mature, price-discovered reverse logistics — and chapter 78 is the only metal chapter where our trade data shows exports exceeding imports.

India imports its recycling feedstock: $8.0bn/yr of copper+aluminium scrap (HS 7404+7602). Domestic EoL collection (EPR, NCMM's Rs.1,500cr scheme, ELV rules) substitutes those imports directly — this is the recyclers' growth runway, not new smelting technology.

Solar PV recycling is the 2035+ opportunity, not a current business: CEEW shows losses of Rs.10,230-12,341/tonne today, flipping positive only with EPR certificate trading for Cu/Ag/Si (+Rs.24,659/t swing) or high-silver TOPCon waste (+Rs.1,125/t) arriving post-2028.
Valuation caveat: the market has already priced the circular-economy tailwind (PE 31-53, P/B 5+ except Nile at 1.9). The business models are validated; the entry prices are not cheap.
